revisions.title: Writing as a reminder, not a substitute
revisions.body: The Egyptian tale turns on a reversal: Theuth presents writing as a drug for memory and wisdom, while Thamus says it produces forgetfulness and only the appearance of wisdom. Socrates later calls writing a reminder for one who already knows, then contrasts its helplessness when questioned with speech written with knowledge in the learner’s soul, capable of defending itself. I hear this as a limit on what writing can do, not its disappearance.
